growth_story.headline: French Polynesia's income per person has grown again since 2014, but in 2024 it was still 25.1 percent below its 1986 peak.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in French Polynesia peaked at 27,814 dollars in 1986. By 2024 it was 20,847 dollars, still 25.1 percent below that peak and lower than in 1965, the first year of the record. From 1990 to 2013 it shrank by 1.3 percent a year on average, a slide that included a 4.6 percent fall in 2009, and the UN sources say little about its causes beyond noting that French nuclear testing ended in 1996. Since 2014, when it reached its low of 18,928 dollars, it has grown by 1.0 percent a year, though the pandemic cut it by 10.6 percent in 2020. The sources credit the return of tourists in 2022 with a rebound in jobs and growth, and growth reached 2.5 percent in 2023 before slowing to 0.9 percent in 2024. They describe a small economy that runs mostly on services, led by tourism, with black pearls its second-largest resource.

threads.title: Tourism carries the recovery
threads.text: Tourism is the territory's main export. Visitor numbers in 2023 passed both their 2019 level and an old record set in 2000, but they barely grew in 2024, the year growth in income per person slowed to 0.9 percent.

threads.title: Pandemic shock and rebound
threads.text: The pandemic hit tourism hard, and income per person fell by 10.6 percent in 2020, the deepest fall in the whole record. The UN papers say the return of tourists in 2022 drove a rebound in jobs and growth.

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2024/7)
citations.quote: The pandemic took a heavy toll on tourism, but it regained its place in the Polynesian economy in 2022.

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2024/7)
citations.quote: the recovery in tourist numbers has contributed significantly to a rebound in the labour market and overall growth in the territorial economy

threads.title: Black pearls after the pandemic
threads.text: Cultured black pearls are the territory's second-largest resource after tourism and most of its exports of local goods. The sector came out of the pandemic weakened, but a sudden rise in demand then pushed pearl export prices to a high not seen for years.

citations.quote: pearl products (the Territory's second-largest own resource after tourism) accounted for three quarters of all revenues from the export of local products in 2023

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2024/7)
citations.quote: Nevertheless, the sector remains weakened by the impact of the pandemic.

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2025/7)

threads.title: Small market, heavy imports
threads.text: The economy runs mostly on services, and its small home market is dominated by large public and private firms, notably in energy and retail. Manufacturing is held back by that small market and depends heavily on imported raw materials and energy.

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2025/7)
citations.quote: Given the small size of the domestic market, the economy is dominated by large public and private companies, particularly in the energy and retail sectors.

citations.title: French Polynesia: Working paper prepared by the Secretariat (A/AC.109/2026/7)
citations.quote: a small domestic market that limits economies of scale and a heavy dependence on imported raw materials and energy products

threads.title: The end of nuclear testing
threads.text: France tested nuclear weapons in the territory from 1966 to 1996, and income per person peaked in 1986, during the last decade of testing. A French parliamentary inquiry published in 2025 looked at the economic legacy, including the state transfers meant to reshape the economy after the tests, but the sources do not measure their effect on growth.

growth_story.tension: The sources say visitor numbers in 2023 and 2024 beat the old record set in 2000, yet income per person in 2024 (20,847 dollars) was still below its 2000 level (22,499 dollars), so record tourism has not brought back earlier incomes.
